title: Unit comparison from an invertible affine closed-site counit
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $V$ an affine small pro-etale object [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ [def-pc-scheme], $I=\ker(A\to\Gamma(V\times_XZ,\mathcal O))$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $B$ be the identity object of the affine ind-etale basis over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Suppose evaluation at $B$ takes epimorphisms of set sheaves to surjections. For any adjunction between the canonical closed-site lift and base change [def-exc-closed-site-lift], an invertible counit at $B$ implies that the actual inverse-image adjunction unit on sections at $V$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No specialization hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BL (1),(2); Tag 09AC, affine reduction and unit identification

proof.text: For an epimorphism of set sheaves at r(B), the affine pro-etale locally-surjective criterion supplies one surjective affine cover q:W -> r(B) and a lift. This singleton is a precoverage cover; v sends it to a cover of v(r(B)). The invertible counit identifies this object with B. Subcanonical Yoneda and projective evaluation split v(q). Since v is fully faithful, its section descends to a section of q. Restriction along that section supplies a lift at r(B). The argument works also for empty affine schemes.

Use precomposition by v followed by sheafification as a left adjoint to restriction along r. Its actual unit at B is restriction along the counit followed by the sheafification unit at r(B). The injectivity and projective-surjectivity lemmas from affine closed inverse-image evaluation prove bijectivity for sets. The natural sheafifyComposeIso comparison with the forgetful functor transfers this to abelian groups. Restriction to the affine bases is an equivalence, so the inverse mate of the direct-image comparison is invertible. The identity unit_mateEquiv_symm therefore proves invertibility of the actual quotient-immersion unit at B.

For a cartesian square with weakly etale horizontal arrows, restriction has a direct-image base-change comparison from Over.pullbackMapComparison. Its rotation on the sites is the composite of pullbackComp and pullbackCongr isomorphisms, verified by the two projection equations. Applying a sheaf computes the corresponding rotated sheaf comparison. Iterated mates identify its inverse mate with the conjugate of this isomorphism; conjugation of adjunctions preserves isomorphisms. The unit mate identity then transfers invertibility of evaluated units from the localized morphism to the original morphism. These calculations are proved as private helpers, adapting the source-library WeaklyEtale base-change calculation to the finite-coefficient imports.

The pullback of the given closed immersion to V is affine and surjective on global sections. The ring first isomorphism theorem constructs its quotient-by-the-actual-kernel coordinate isomorphism; naturality of isoSpec proves the projection identity. Transport the cartesian pullback square through the two coordinate isomorphisms. Its horizontal arrows are weakly etale. Apply the localized-unit result to the identity object over Spec A, using the quotient result above. Evaluation at the resulting pro-etale object is naturally isomorphic to evaluation at V. Pointwise invertibility in F proves invertibility of the natural transformation in the statement.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09BL and 09AC; complete Lean proof using singleton-cover projectivity, affine sheafification units, quotient coordinates and weakly etale localization mates. Site mate calculation adapted from WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.BaseChange.WeaklyEtale.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_proEtaleUnit_sections_of_closedSiteCounit
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (V : X.ProEt) [IsAffine V.left]
 :
    let A := Γ(V.left, ⊤)
    let I := RingHom.ker (pullback.fst V.hom i).appTop.hom
    let B := AffineProEt.ofEtale (𝟙 (Spec A))
    (∀ (P Q : Sheaf (AffineProEt.topology (Spec A)) (Type (u + 1))) (φ : P ⟶ Q),
      Epi φ → Function.Surjective (φ.hom.app (op B))) →
    ∀ adj : AffineProEt.closedSiteLift A I ⊣ AffineProEt.closedSiteBaseChange A I,
      IsIso (adj.counit.app B) →
      IsIso (Functor.whiskerRight (proEtaleSheafAdjunction i AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).unit
        ((sheafSections (ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (op V)))
